risk_if_not_implemented: Without Security, Compliance & Resilience Representative for Asset Lifecycle Changes, unauthorized, untested or undocumented changes may introduce vulnerabilities, instability or loss of system integrity. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Unaddressed Security / Compliance Exposure (R-GV-2), Unperformed / Unowned Control Responsibilities (R-GV-3), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Emergency Changes
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to govern change management procedures for "emergency" changes.
compensating_control_1.justification: Emergency Changes (CHG-10) provides change management discipline that compensates for the absence of Security, Compliance & Resilience Representative for Asset Lifecycle Changes (CHG-05) by ensuring changes to systems and configurations are controlled and reviewed to prevent unintended security impacts. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Dual Approval For High-Impact Environments
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to require dual approval for any changes that might result in a serious incident that could adversely impact:
(1) Business processes; and/or
(2) Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD).
compensating_control_2.justification: Dual Approval For High-Impact Environments (CHG-04.4) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Security, Compliance & Resilience Representative for Asset Lifecycle Changes (CHG-05) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
